name: Cloud with Rain
tldr: 🌧️ reports rainy weather, while adding a gloomy mood to everyday conversations and bad-news reactions.

contextMeanings.meaning: 🌧️ states that it is raining or that rain is expected.
contextMeanings.example: bring an umbrella, it's raining outside 🌧️

contextMeanings.meaning: 🌧️ can jokingly suggest that a situation has become depressing or that someone's plans are being spoiled.
contextMeanings.example: traffic, cancelled plans, and low battery all at once 🌧️

contextMeanings.meaning: 🌧️ can exaggerate a minor annoyance as though the whole day has turned into a dreary downpour.
🌧️ functions as a quick weather note when rain may affect travel, outdoor work, or an event.
contextMeanings.example: the site visit will be delayed by heavy rain 🌧️

platformNotes.note: 🌧️ reads naturally as a visual reaction in a comment or caption, especially when the video itself shows gloomy or rainy scenes. Its small blue raindrops add mood without requiring an explanation.
In captions and comments, 🌧️ can reinforce a melancholy aesthetic or a low-key complaint. Without surrounding text, people may simply take it as a reference to the weather in a photo.

In a direct message, 🌧️ works well for a literal heads-up about rain and can soften a complaint about unpleasant conditions. A question such as "should I bring a jacket? 🌧️" makes the practical meaning clear.
🌧️ is clearest in workplace channels when it accompanies information about travel, deliveries, or outdoor plans. Used alone in a serious channel, it may seem like an unnecessary decorative reaction.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z may use 🌧️ as a low-key reaction image when a situation feels dreary or disappointing. On video-focused platforms, the reaction can be understood before the weather itself is considered.
Millennials are likely to read 🌧️ literally when it appears in a weather update, but may also accept it as a muted mood marker when someone is describing a bad day.
Gen X generally gives 🌧️ its plain weather meaning, especially in practical exchanges about commuting or errands. A sarcastic use should have enough context to make that interpretation unmistakable.

warnings.title: Mistaking a mood for a forecast
warnings.description: Someone using 🌧️ to complain about a disappointing day may be interpreted as making a literal weather statement. Add words such as "today is really" or use another emoji when the mood is the point.

warnings.title: Sending it in serious situations
warnings.description: 🌧️ can appear flippant when used beside genuine loss, illness, or workplace trouble. Send plain, direct language in those conversations instead of relying on the emoji to soften the news.

seoDescription: What does 🌧️ mean? It reports rainy weather and can add a gloomy, disappointed mood to everyday messages, complaints, and reactions.

longForm.overview:
🌧️ is the rain-cloud emoji, and its most dependable job is to say that rain is present or expected. That makes it more specific than ☁️, which can mean overcast skies without precipitation, and less dramatic than ⛈️, which includes a thunderstorm. 🌦️ is the closer neighbour when sunshine and rain are happening together; 🌧️ gives the scene a steadier, fully rainy appearance.

In ordinary messages, the emoji also works as a small mood picture. A person may use it to make a disappointing update feel more rueful than dramatic, or to react to a chain of minor mishaps without writing a complaint. The meaning comes from the combination of a grey cloud and falling rain: things are not cheerful, but the sender is usually commenting rather than asking for help. The emoji does not inherently signal romance, hostility, or sadness, so surrounding words matter. A weather forecast, a travel delay, and a joking reaction can all use 🌧️ successfully because its image is broad enough to carry each tone.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🌧️ usually appears in short, practical exchanges: "parking is flooded 🌧️," "the walk will take longer 🌧️," or "rain tomorrow 🌧️." People add it when a forecast affects an outing, commute, delivery, or outdoor event, allowing the picture to do some of the work. It can also trail a complaint, where it turns an annoying sequence of events into a visual summary of a bad day.

The less literal use is playful rather than intensely emotional. Someone might send 🌧️ after dropping their phone in the sink, losing a train, or forgetting an important item. The rain cloud makes the reaction feel weary and mildly self-mocking. It is not usually a substitute for explaining what happened, and it lands better when the preceding sentence already supplies the joke.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not use 🌧️ when the recipient needs clear information about safety, travel, or a serious disruption. In a message about flooding, a storm, or an accident, a decorative emoji can make the warning look less urgent. Write the location, timing, and required action plainly, then add 🌧️ only if it does not compete with the information.

It is also a poor choice beside grief, illness, or another painful disclosure because the gloom can appear to trivialize the subject. People who take the glyph literally may think the sender is discussing the weather, while others may read the emoji as an unwanted mood cue. Use ordinary text instead. If the intended feeling is specifically gloomy but not serious, pair 🌧️ with words that establish the joke, such as "my weekend 🌧️" or "everything went wrong 🌧️."
longForm.howToReply:
Match the literal message with a practical answer: "how far away is the rain? 🌧️," "I can delay the delivery," or "take the covered route." If 🌧️ was attached to a complaint, reply to the actual mishap with sympathy or humor rather than repeating the emoji mechanically. "At least you didn't lock your keys in there too" continues the bad-day joke without treating the weather as a forecast.

To keep a reaction playful, you can answer with another gloomy weather emoji, but that works best when the exchange is already informal. If it lands on your own bad-news post, ask whether the sender meant the situation literally or was making a joke. For a serious problem, replace the emoji with a direct question about what they need, such as "are you okay?" or "do you need help getting there?"

faqs.question: What does 🌧️ mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: 🌧️ normally means it is raining, either literally or as a gloomy reaction. If the message has no weather context, it is not a reliable sign of romantic interest.

faqs.question: Is 🌧️ flirty?
faqs.answer: 🌧️ is not inherently flirty. It can appear in a romantic conversation as a weather reference or a playful mood, but the surrounding message determines the intention.

faqs.question: What does 🌧️ mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: On TikTok, 🌧️ commonly accompanies rainy visuals, melancholy clips, or joking reactions to annoying situations. It may be understood as a mood picture before anyone considers the literal weather.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 🌧️ and ☁️?
faqs.answer: 🌧️ specifically includes falling rain, while ☁️ represents a cloud and can indicate an overcast sky without actual precipitation. Use 🌧️ when the rain matters.

conversationExamples.message: the rain starts right when we pick our table 🌧️
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a lighthearted observation about the weather during a date, not necessarily a romantic symbol. Reply by talking about the restaurant, the walk, or whether the rain is worth staying for.

conversationExamples.message: missed the bus, forgot my umbrella, and the fit is bad too 🌧️
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is using 🌧️ to summarize a gloomy run of small disasters. A sympathetic joke about the day will fit better than weather advice.

conversationExamples.message: the warehouse handoff is delayed because of rain 🌧️
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is primarily a practical workplace update about rain affecting the schedule. Confirm the new timing and any operational impact.

conversationExamples.message: it's pouring, so we're staying in and ordering dinner 🌧️
conversationExamples.interpretation: The emoji explains why the family plan changed without making the update sound alarming. Respond by asking what they ordered or when the rain is expected to ease.

conversationExamples.message: photos from the trip are somehow all grey and wet 🌧️
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is wryly commenting on disappointing weather during a trip. You can join the joke or ask for one of the less rainy pictures.
